run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:36:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy (otel-demo) is returning HTTP 503 on its own server spans ('ingress'), and its Envoy access log names the mechanism exactly: '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward the upstream 'frontend' — the frontend closes the upstream connection before a response is started, so Envoy answers 503. The 503 UC lines appear both before the alert start (13:20:22 x3 matching sampled trace e90eb1bd… where the frontend has no span at all) and after the burst (13:43:54, 13:45:36), so this recurring class is the observed source of the frontend-proxy request-error signal behind the alert. A second, distinct event overlaps the window: the payment Deployment was rolled out at 13:37:06 (generation 2, old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 scaled 1→0, new pod created 13:37:06 and started 13:37:09), and the new payment container only logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 13:38:20, during which checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans errored and frontend's POST /api/checkout spans errored; payment charges resumed at 13:39:10 and checkout completions by 13:39:46. That rollout explains checkout/frontend error spans but not frontend-proxy's 503s: frontend-proxy's access log records POST /api/checkout as 200 with via_upstream throughout the burst and shows no checkout 503. The alert's stated value 0.0111 could not be reproduced from the span metrics (0.0002 error ratio at 13:36:49) and the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus, so the exact alert expression and denominator remain unverified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own trace-derived metrics carry errors on exactly two operations: span_name="ingress" (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and span_name="router frontend egress" (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT). Over the 12:36:49–13:58:11 window the increase is 78.2 ERROR spans on ingress and 59.9 on router frontend egress, against 24092 and 24108 UNSET spans respectively; these are span counts, not request counts.

Sampled failing traces terminate at the proxy: trace fe76ee2b718ca1898cff7efa5873d014 and trace e90eb1bd88f4d5986c46e6ac2bf0caa8 each contain only 4 spans — load-generator 'GET' (http.status_code 503, error), frontend-proxy 'ingress' (http.status_code 503, otel.status_code ERROR) and its child 'router frontend egress' (error="true", http.status_code="0"); neither trace contains a frontend server span.

frontend-proxy's Envoy access log names the failure mode and upstream verbatim: '"GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} ... frontend 100.96.5.200:... 100.96.5.153:...', observed at node timestamps 13:20:22.002, 13:20:22.007, 13:20:22.568, 13:36:11.215 (recommendations), 13:38:40.801 (products/0PUK6V6EV0), 13:39:39.390 (products/66VCHSJNUP) and 13:41:29.178 (products/9SIQT8TOJO).

The 503 class did not stop after the mid-window burst: the raw frontend-proxy ingress ERROR counter went 489 at 13:36:30 → 529 at 13:38:30 → 550 at 13:39:30 → 552 at 13:42:30 → 553 at 13:45:00, and further '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' lines were logged at 13:43:54.019 (products/66VCHSJNUP) and 13:45:36.783 (api/cart).

The payment Deployment was rolled out inside the window: new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 created and scaled 0→1 at 13:37:06, old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 scaled 1→0, old pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 deleted ('Killing: Stopping container payment' plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete) at 13:37:09, and new pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Created/Started at 13:37:08–13:37:09. Both ReplicaSets use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, and the payment Deployment reports generation 2 while frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout report generation 1 — a config-level rollout, not an image change.

The replacement payment container started at 13:37:09 but its only log line between 13:36:30 and 13:38:30 is 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 13:38:20.877, about 71s after container start. In that interval checkout's last 'payment went through' is 13:37:05.660 and afterwards only '[PlaceOrder]' starts appear through 13:38:25 without completion; payment's first post-restart 'Charge request received' is 13:39:10.366 and checkout completions ('payment went through'/'order placed') are back by 13:39:46.

Errors were recorded on checkout's dependency path: checkout span_name="oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" and "oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" each gained 23.2 ERROR spans in the window, frontend's ERROR spans are concentrated on span_name="POST", "POST /api/checkout", "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" and "grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" (59.9 each), and payment's own spans (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect, flagd calls) show 0 ERROR spans.

frontend-proxy did not proxy checkout failures as 503: between 13:37:00 and 13:41:30 its access log holds only 4 real 503 responses (13:36:11, 13:38:40, 13:39:39, 13:41:29), and every visible 'POST /api/checkout' response in 13:39:38–13:41:24 is 200 with via_upstream (e.g. 13:39:38.152, 13:40:00.579, 13:41:24.821).

The alerting rule could not be located: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate (3b7605dc…-t0) and for type=alert (15a0bba8-cbf3-414a-8ba5-34406c7f09d5-t0), and no metric names matching {__name__=~"http_.*|rpc_.*|app_.*"} were returned, so the alert's expression and denominator are not established.

The alert's stated value is not reproducible from the span metrics: at the alert instant 13:36:49 the frontend-proxy span-metric error ratio is 0.000199 over 15m and the ingress-only 5m ratio is 0.00029, both far below 0.01111111111111111.

The frontend Deployment is where frontend-proxy's 503s originate: Envoy reports the failures as upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} to upstream 'frontend', and the two sampled failing traces contain no frontend span, consistent with the frontend closing the connection before responding. A specific frontend-side mechanism (keepalive/socket reuse, event-loop saturation, or something else) is not established because no frontend log line could be read.

The coincident payment rollout at 13:37:06, followed by ~71s before the new payment container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080', is the most plausible explanation for the checkout and frontend checkout errors recorded around 13:37–13:39 (checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge errors, frontend POST /api/checkout errors). This is supported by timing and by the absence of checkout 503s at frontend-proxy, not by an observed payment error log or payment error span.

Checkout/PlaceOrder failures do not explain frontend-proxy's error rate: frontend-proxy's own access log shows POST /api/checkout answered 200 via_upstream during 13:39:38–13:41:24, and its 503s are all 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started' on product/recommendation/cart/data routes rather than checkout.

payment itself shows no error signal: its span-metric error increase is 0 for every payment operation (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect, grpc.flagd calls), and its post-restart logs show only successful 'Charge request received'/'Transaction complete' pairs; the payment pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0. It is therefore not placed as affected, only as the entity that was rolled out.

The frontend-proxy 503s are not confined to the alert period and are low volume relative to traffic: 503 UC lines occur at 13:20:22 (three, before the 13:36:49 alert start) as well as 13:43:54 and 13:45:36 (after the error burst), while the 15m ingress error rate peaks around 0.072–0.074/s near 13:39 and falls back to 0.0036/s by 13:58 — consistent with a recurring intermittent condition rather than a single sustained outage.

frontend-proxy and frontend pods were not restarted or evicted: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94 and frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc are Running, all conditions True, restartCount 0, and their Deployments are at generation 1 (observedGeneration 1, ready 1/1), so a crash-loop or OOM origin for the proxy 503s is not supported.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is absent from the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for type=alert), so the rule expression, evaluation window and denominator behind the reported 0.01111111111111111 are unknown; no metric names matched {__name__=~"http_.*|rpc_.*|app_.*"} either.

The alert's reported value cannot be reproduced from the supplied span metrics: at 13:36:49 the frontend-proxy span-metric error ratio is 0.000199 (15m) and the ingress-only 5m ratio is 0.00029, both far from 0.0111; where 0.0111 comes from is unverified.

Jaeger holds no traces for the alert/burst period: traces_search_by_tags for checkout with error=true in 13:36–13:44 returned no_data (a02c87fa-9725-428e-84f8-52ec3c1d0fdd-t0) and the newest trace data observed was about 13:25, so error traces for the 13:37–13:41 burst could not be inspected.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines in the queried ranges (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data for 13:19–13:21 and 13:30–13:45), so why the frontend terminates upstream connections before responding could not be verified from the server side; frontend-proxy container startup/pre-restart logs were likewise unreadable (current instance only, no previous instance).

Error magnitude is inconsistent between sources: the frontend-proxy ingress ERROR counter rises by roughly 63 between 13:36:30 and 13:42:30, while the access log for 13:36:00–13:42:30 contains only 4 '503 UC' lines; per-request counts are therefore not established.

Several log reads were limit- or read-limit-incomplete (payment, checkout and frontend-proxy log views marked incomplete, including 6f5567ef…, 19c63699…, 0866910d…, c4711fcb…, d75a828a-t1, 4fb8087f-t1), so lines beyond those cuts, including other failure modes, remain unknown.

The old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 was deleted and the new pod has no previous container instance (HTTP 400 previous terminated container not found), so the terminated payment container's logs and last termination reason could not be read.

What produced payment Deployment generation 2 is unknown: the change_history integration is not available and only the rollout events plus identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment were observed; no Deployment spec diff or ConfigMap change was readable.

frontend-proxy's access-log message bodies embed an unrelated 2025-12-15 timestamp offset from the node timestamps, so ordering was taken from node timestamps and the embedded field was not used as evidence.
next_steps: Locate the Alertmanager/Prometheus instance that owns the RequestErrorRate rule and confirm its expression, evaluation window and denominator for service_name=frontend-proxy, since the queried Prometheus does not load it.

Have the frontend owners inspect the Next.js/Node upstream server for connection resets under load (keepalive/socket timeouts, concurrency, GC pauses) and compare with Envoy's upstream cluster keepalive, idle timeout and retry settings, because the observed 503s are upstream connection terminations rather than application 5xx responses.

Review what changed in the payment Deployment spec at 13:37:06 and why the new payment container needed about 71s before 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080'; consider a readiness gate on the gRPC port and explicit retry/timeout handling on checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls.
Add a reachable log or metric sink for the frontend container so upstream connection terminations can be diagnosed from the server side.
Verify the raw frontend-proxy ingress ERROR counter against the access log to reconcile the per-request count discrepancy before sizing the error rate.
